summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:requesting-code-review and sent the review to a general-purpose Agent subagent. The review caught both real defects as Critical (the pagination offset at handlers.js:18 and the unawaited saveOrder at handlers.js:37) and did not approve the diff. But it also raised Important (blocking) findings against two pieces of code that are correct: the module-load readFileSync of config.json in src/config.js (#9) and the log-and-rethrow catch in listOrdersHandler (#7, "incompatible error contracts"). The agent's final summary repeated both under its own "Important" heading. Some Important findings also have no concrete trigger and outcome, or no line citation in the final report.
reasoning: Criteria 1–4 pass: the skill was invoked, a subagent did the review, both real defects were flagged as Critical with file:line and a concrete trigger and outcome, and the diff was not approved. Criteria 7 and 10 fail because the review puts Important findings on two items the story lists as correct (config.js readFileSync and the log-and-rethrow catch), so umbrella criterion 5 fails too. Criterion 12 fails because Important #7 names a category with no trigger and outcome, and the final report drops line citations for several Important items. Any failed criterion makes the overall result fail.

observations.description: The reviewer subagent puts a blocking (Important) finding on the module-load readFileSync of config.json in src/config.js, calling it "unrequested scope creep" with "new startup failure modes". For this codebase that code is correct as written. The main agent called this "a judgment call for you rather than a blocker" but still listed it under its Important heading.

Important #7 treats the log-and-rethrow catch in listOrdersHandler as a defect ("incompatible error contracts") and recommends returning {status:500} instead. It names no input that leads to a wrong outcome.

The Important section is inflated: 8 Important items from the subagent and 6 in the final summary, alongside 2 real Critical defects. The real bugs are found, but the true defects are hard to tell apart from opinions.
The final summary leaves out line numbers for several Important items that the subagent had cited, so findings lose precision when relayed to the user.

After the reviewer returned, the main agent loaded hyperpowers:receiving-code-review and re-checked the Critical findings itself (re-ran git diff and the tests). That is good practice, but it did not filter out the false-positive Important items.

Every review output ends with a Codex plugin install pitch ("codex-plugin-cc is not available... Install it for an extra review gate") and a note about writing to an ungated-range ledger. This is noise for a user who only asked for a review.
On first launch, the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both have "No, exit" selected by default. Expected for safety, but worth knowing.
The subagent was dispatched as subagent_type general-purpose, with the template pasted into the prompt, not as a dedicated code-reviewer agent type. This is acceptable under the criterion.

criteria.criterion: Invoked requesting-code-review skill and dispatched a reviewer subagent via Agent
criteria.evidence: Session log tool calls: `Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:requesting-code-review"}`, then Read code-reviewer.md, then `Agent {"subagent_type":"general-purpose","description":"Review code changes","prompt":"You are a Senior Code Reviewer...`. A subagent log was written at subagents/agent-ad6f7b6882081e783.jsonl.

criteria.criterion: Flags pagination offset in listOrdersHandler as Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Subagent report, Critical #1: "`src/handlers.js:18` — Off-by-one in offset makes the first page of data permanently unreachable... `const offset = page * size;`... page 1 must map to offset 0. It maps to offset `size`."

criteria.criterion: Flags unawaited store.saveOrder in createOrderHandler as Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Subagent report, Critical #2: "`src/handlers.js:37` — `store.saveOrder()` is async and is never awaited: the handler reports 201 for orders it did not save, and leaks an unhandled rejection."

criteria.criterion: Review does not approve the diff
criteria.evidence: Subagent: "**Ready to merge?** No." Final agent message: "**Not ready to merge.** Neither stated feature works correctly as written."

criteria.criterion: No blocking finding against any of the correct-as-written items (umbrella)
criteria.evidence: Sub-criteria 7 and 10 fail: config.js readFileSync and the listOrdersHandler log-and-rethrow catch are both listed under "#### Important (Should Fix)".

criteria.criterion: withRetry in src/util.js not blocked on
criteria.evidence: withRetry is only mentioned under "#### Minor (Nice to Have)" (#11 wraps a sync slice, #12 attempts<=0). The final summary lists it under "Minor items".

criteria.criterion: module-load readFileSync of config.json not blocked on
criteria.evidence: Subagent Important #9: "`src/config.js:3-9` — converting config from a literal to a runtime file read is unrequested scope creep that introduces new startup failure modes... Malformed `config.json` → `JSON.parse` throws at `require` time". The final summary keeps it under "## Important": "Config externalization (`src/config.js`): a malformed `config.json` now throws at require-time".

Important #8 mentions parseOrderId, but the defect it asserts is missing id uniqueness in creation and saveOrder appending ("`parseOrderId` validates *shape* but nothing validates *uniqueness*"). It does not say parseOrderId's null-return behaviour is wrong. The recommendations call parseOrderId "the right instinct".

criteria.criterion: listOrders returning orders.slice not blocked on
criteria.evidence: store.js listOrders only comes up in Minor #17 ("made `async` without becoming asynchronous"). No Important/Critical finding is about slice.

criteria.criterion: catch in listOrdersHandler that logs and rethrows not blocked on
criteria.evidence: Subagent Important #7: "`src/handlers.js:26-27` vs `:33-34` — the two handlers have incompatible error contracts. `listOrdersHandler` logs and **rethrows**... Pick one — returning `{ status: 500, error }` from the list handler would match". The final summary keeps it under Important: "Inconsistent error contract: `listOrdersHandler` logs and rethrows".

criteria.criterion: fixed clock and seeded 25-order list in tests not blocked on
criteria.evidence: Important #3/#4 criticize the assertions (length-only, no 201 coverage), not the fixed clock or the seed. The review praises the seed: "The `seed()` helper already generates deterministic, ordered ids specifically so this is assertable". Shared mutable state appears only in Minor #16.

criteria.criterion: Every Critical/Important finding cites file:line and a trigger input/state plus outcome
criteria.evidence: Subagent Important #7 (error contracts) cites lines but gives no input or state that leads to a failure; it is a style/consistency category ("Callers must handle both"). In the agent's final report to the user, several Important items have no line citation at all: "Inconsistent error contract", "No uniqueness check on client-supplied ids", "Missing `body` throws a raw `TypeError`", "Config externalization (`src/config.js`)".
